page.layout: One column of running text, full width. No marginal notes. Running head at top centre, page number at top left. Catchword at bottom right.

main_text.p: sive Veterum Latinorum authoritate sive alio, ut videtur, motus argumento, secus de hac Epistolâ, ut de Catholicis quibusdam aliis aliquando sensit; adeò vir penè divinus & dotibus supra humanam sortem instructus, hîc, ut in aliis, hu-mani nihil à se alienum ostendit.

III. Magnum sanè divinæ & immotæ originis argumentū, quò majores ad subvertendam eam & validiores impetus fecit hostis ille humani generis. Et quem-admodum vix pars ulla Canonis tot ini-qua hominum judicia experta est, ita vix ulla Canonicis notis illustrior, magisque cœlestem spirans originem. Sive atten-dimus doctrinæ genus excelsum, de Chri-sti divinitate, incarnatione, sacerdotio, figuris quæ sive in Aarone, sive Melchise-deco, sive typis legalibus ac ceremoniis præcesserant, quæque sublimius quid sonant humanâ sapientia; sive expendimus sanctissima vitæ instituta, ac morum præ-cepta; sive majorem omni exceptione cum Scripturis utriusque Fœderis con-sensum, in historicis frustrà nonnullis im-

page.notes: The running head and text are set in a roman face with long s; long s is normalised to s. The words "historicis" and "frustrà" appear in italic type; "nonnullis" may be set slightly heavier, but I read it as roman. The final word "impetu-" is split across the page, and the catchword "peti-" is the start of the next page. The "III." opening the second paragraph is a numbered thesis and is therefore a paragraph, not a heading. The scan is slightly blurred at the top right corner, but all words were legible.
